title: Apollo 2: Delivery Service
tagline: Prove that a small lander can carry real science to the Moon.

goal.text: Deliver a science payload to the south pole and switch it on
goal.why: Commercial deliveries let NASA put instruments on the Moon faster and more often

facts.text: Through Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS), NASA works with American companies to deliver scientific, exploration and technology payloads to the Moon's surface and orbit.
NASA describes the Moon Base as humanity's first lunar outpost, a place where astronauts will live, work and explore near the Moon's South Pole.
LRO has been studying the Moon from up close since 2009, making it the longest-lived lunar orbiting mission ever.

candidate_sites.name: Shackleton Rim
candidate_sites.why: Sunlight for most of the day keeps the lander warm and powered

candidate_sites.name: Connecting Ridge
candidate_sites.why: A high ridge with an open sky for radio links

ship.rationale: A small commercial lander has little spare mass, so every part must earn its place and the instruments must stay powered.

items.prompt: Which part keeps the lander's computers running in the dark?
Where is the Moon Base planned?

cruise.story: The radio link to Earth dropped. Line the antenna back up with the signal.
We drifted off course. Line up the rings to correct our path.
Small debris ahead. Steer the ship through the gaps.

tasks.title: Walk to the instrument spot
tasks.hint: Follow the flat, bright ground away from the lander

tasks.title: Set up the radio relay
tasks.hint: Pick a spot with a clear view of Earth

tasks.title: Switch on the instruments
tasks.hint: Sweep the scanner until the signal locks

voice_lines.text: Apollo 2, Houston. This is a delivery mission: get the instruments to the pole safely and switch them on.
Apollo 2, all systems go. Launch when ready.
Apollo 2, choose a flat spot. A gentle landing keeps the science safe.
Apollo 2, the instruments are alive and talking to Earth. Nicely done.
